paragraphs: The first: the statement of Scripture, Gen 18:22, "and Abraham stood yet before the Lord." They claim it was originally "and the Lord stood yet before Abraham." They argue this from the narrative-context: Gen 18:1, "and the Lord appeared unto him"; v. 2, "and he lifted up his eyes and looked." [On their reading,] Abraham asked God to stand still while he prepared a service to perform — for he says (v. 3), "if I have found favor in thine eyes, pass not, I pray, from thy servant." When he was done with his hospitality and they had finished, Scripture reports (v. 22), "and they turned from there and went their way [toward Sodom]" — and the report that God Himself stood, until the end — that is what "and the Lord stood yet before Abraham" is taken to mean.

Case 2: Num 11:15, "and if thou wilt deal thus with me, kill me, I pray thee"; "and let me not see my wretchedness" — they say my wretchedness was originally "thy wretchedness." Case 3: Num 12:12, "let her not be as one dead" — they say "her" was originally "us"; "let her not be as one of whom, when he comes out of his mother's womb, half his flesh is consumed" — they say "his mother's" was originally "our mother's," and "his flesh" was originally "our flesh." Their justification: brother is "the flesh of his brother," per Gen 37:27, "for he is our brother, our flesh." Case 4: Num 16:14, "wilt thou put out the eyes of these men?" — they say "of these men" was originally "thine eyes." Case 5: 1 Sam 3:13, "for the iniquity which he knoweth, because his sons made themselves contemptible" — they say "his sons" was originally "my sons"; "upon themselves" was originally "upon Me." They argue from 1 Sam 2:29, "Why do ye trample on My sacrifices and My offerings?"; "and thou honourest thy sons above Me"; and v. 30, "for them that honour Me I will honour, and they that despise Me shall be lightly esteemed." Case 6: 2 Sam 16:12, "peradventure the Lord will look on my affliction" — they say "on my affliction" was originally "with His eye."[{2}] Case 7: 1 Kgs 12:16, "To your tents, O Israel" and parallel 2 Chr 10:16 — they say "tents" was originally "gods"; and "and Israel went to their tents" was originally "to their God."

Case 8: Ezek 8:17, "and lo, they put the branch to their nose" — was "to My nose."[{3}] Case 9 (Cairo numbering skips to "the tenth"): Hab 1:12, "art thou not from everlasting, O Lord my God, my Holy One? we shall not die" — was "thou shalt not die." Case 10: Mal 1:13, "and ye said: What a weariness this is! and ye snuffed at it" — was "at Me." Case 11: Zech 2:12, "for he who touches you touches the apple of his eye" — was "my eye." Case 12: Jer 2:11, "but my people hath exchanged its glory" — was "my glory." Case 13: Hos 4:7, "therefore will I change their glory into shame" — was "my glory." Case 14: Job 7:20, "so that I am become a burden to myself" — was "to thyself." Case 15: Job 32:3, "because they had not found an answer, yet had condemned Job" — was originally "they had condemned God."[{4}] Case 16: Lam 3:20, "my soul hath them still in remembrance, and is bowed down within me" — was "thy soul" and "is bowed in thee." Case 17: Ps 106:20, "they exchanged their glory" — was "my glory."[{5}] ---
